scenes.title: Preschooler turning away and covering eyes with both hands beside a single white marshmallow and silver desk bell
scenes.era: 1970, Stanford Bing Nursery School 'Surprise Room', Palo Alto

layout.description: Minimalist sunlit 1970 preschool testing room with bare cream walls, a child-sized wooden table and chair, a small white paper plate holding one fluffy white marshmallow, a shiny chrome call bell, and an observation mirror.

positions.who: Preschooler mannequin (child-proportioned matte-white mannequin in 1970 overalls and striped tee)
positions.where: sitting sideways on the wooden chair, leaning far back from the plate and covering eyes playfully with both palms to avoid looking at the marshmallow
positions.facing: turned away from the center plate

positions.who: Walter Mischel (mannequin in 1970 turtleneck and tweed jacket)
positions.where: visible behind the observation glass noting gaze-aversion seconds on a stopwatch

props.name: white paper plate with one white marshmallow
props.period_detail: plain 6-inch paper plate centered on the small wooden table
props.physical_behavior: sits untouched as long as the child's gaze stays averted

props.name: chrome call-back desk bell
props.period_detail: classic small silver tap bell beside the plate
props.physical_behavior: if tapped early, brings the adult back immediately but forfeits the second marshmallow

props.name: opaque metal cake-tin cover on side shelf
props.period_detail: round brushed-tin cover used in the hidden-reward condition
props.physical_behavior: stretches average wait time from 1.03 minutes to 11.29 minutes

actions.verb_sequence: glances once at the marshmallow and silver bell -> slides chair slightly sideways -> covers eyes with both hands and taps toes rhythmically to pass the time
logs strategic gaze aversion passing the 11-minute mark

reactions.reaction: perks up triumphantly when the door clicks open at 15:00 with the second marshmallow
smiles realizing self-control works by starving temptation of attention

scenes.wardrobe: 1970 California preschooler in corduroy overalls and striped shirt; researcher in 1970 tweed blazer over dark turtleneck.
scenes.lighting: Clean, bright California morning daylight in an uncluttered room.
scenes.recognition_hook: Staring straight at the marshmallow breaks kids in sixty-two seconds — covering their eyes or hiding the plate stretches patience tenfold.

key_visual.description: a 1970 preschooler mannequin on a small wooden chair covering its eyes and turning sideways away from a white marshmallow and silver desk bell on a bare table

scenes.title: Uncovered staring condition collapses in 62 seconds

layout.description: Same small table with TWO uncovered treats sitting right under a child's chin.

positions.where: propping chin in both hands six inches from the uncovered marshmallow

actions.verb_sequence: stares unblinkingly at the treat -> reaches out and slaps the silver bell at 62 seconds

reactions.reaction: crosses out his own prediction that seeing the reward helps waiting

scenes.recognition_hook: White-knuckle staring at an uncovered treat collapsed waiting to barely one minute.

scenes.title: 2013 Reliability Twist: Broken vs Kept Art-Supply Promise

layout.description: Bright play table with either a worn two-crayon cup ('sorry, I broke my promise') or a huge shiny art set ('just like I promised!') before the marshmallow plate arrives.

positions.where: setting down the promised deluxe art caddy accurately
nodding with calm trust before the 12-minute marshmallow wait

props.name: deluxe art caddy vs tiny worn crayon cup
props.physical_behavior: quadruples subsequent marshmallow waiting from 3 minutes to 12 minutes

actions.verb_sequence: delivers the exact promised art set -> sets down the marshmallow -> child waits calmly for 12 minutes

reactions.reaction: trusts the adult's word that waiting will actually pay off

scenes.wardrobe: Modern casual lab sweater and child tee.
scenes.recognition_hook: When adults keep their promises first, kids wait four times longer — proving delay is rational trust, not fixed DNA.

scenes.title: Opaque pantry cover & phone-in-another-room setup

layout.description: Clean sunlit study desk where a smartphone goes inside a closed wooden drawer while deep work begins.

positions.where: sliding smartphone into a closed side drawer and opening a clean notebook

props.name: closed wooden desk drawer
props.period_detail: acts just like Mischel's 11-minute opaque cover
props.physical_behavior: removes the hot visual cue effortlessly

actions.verb_sequence: places phone inside opaque drawer -> writes smoothly without willpower strain

reactions.reaction: works calmly with zero bell-ringing urge

scenes.recognition_hook: Out of sight beats iron grit ten to one.
